_comment: The terrain palette — the ONLY place a terrain's look is written down.
Replaces three tables that had drifted apart: TERRAIN_TYPES (dev panel),
TERRAIN_FILL (minimap) and TOS_TERRAIN_FILL (tablet). They disagreed on
exactly one value — redrock, #9e4a30 in the dev panel against #6f3524 in the
game — so for 2,996 tiles the map an author painted was not the map a player
saw. The game's value is canonical here: players are the audience.
Nothing reads this file at runtime. content:import feeds it to deriveWorld,
which resolves every tile into zone_render.spec; renderers read only that.
See docs/proposals/map-pipeline-spec.md §1.2 and §7.
fill              map/minimap background for the tile
text              glyph colour, when the terrain dictates one (road markings).
null lets the renderer pick by luminance, as it does today.
glyph             marker fallback. null = blank tile, which is what painted
ground looks like now: a seamless expanse, marker dropped.
minimap_class     CSS class suffix the game client applies (terr-<class>)
auto_tile         adjacency-aware art (the road connector SVGs)
speed_mult        movement pacing. THE fix for a live bug: pacing keyed off
flags.icon matching /^road_/, so 55 of 158 painted road
tiles carried no speed-up at all.
EVERY VALUE HERE IS A DEFAULT, and a tile's own marker/color/bg_color beats
it — always, on every terrain, with no exception list. `authored_bg_wins`
used to name the three terrains (grass, water, underwater) where a tile was
allowed to win. It was not protecting a second meaning; it was protecting
against the pre-terrain bulk fill sitting in the same column, and it cost
3,484 authored fills. That fill is cleared and the key is gone; see
scripts/content/tile-override-cleanup.mjs and
docs/proposals/tile-presentation-overrides.md.
WATER, GRASS AND UNDERWATER ARE WHAT THAT FLIP LEFT BEHIND. The cleanup
spared their 1,374 fills because those fills were rendering — its warranty
was zero pixel delta. But 'authored beats palette' then meant the terrain
painter did nothing visible on the whole bay and every lawn: repaint one and
the fill would not move, because the tile's own colour was answering. The
fill each of the three carried is now the palette's, and the tiles carrying
exactly that value have given the column back (tile-fill-to-palette.mjs).
Same three warnings apply as to redrock above: these are the values PLAYERS
see, so they are the ones that are canonical. Water's new #1d3b52 is the same
value as WATER_VOID_FILL in the game's minimap, which paints the bay BEYOND
the map's rim — the palette was the only thing in the stack that thought open
water was #3f7fb0. The shading variants — a second
blue on 258 water tiles, a pale strand on 66 grass — stayed authored, because
a colour that differs from its terrain on purpose is what the override is FOR.
SEWER is the last of the marker-decoration cleanups. The Under's 117 tiles were
the only painted-ground-shaped expanse in the world with no terrain at all, so
the map's terrain branch never fired for any of them: they kept their tile
borders and drew a hand-authored box-drawing connector (═ ║ ╬ …) per tile. That
is the same thing the 860 grass/water decorations were — a texture carried
per-tile because the palette had nowhere to put it — and it is deleted the same
way. The tunnel run is now the painted expanse itself, exactly as a road is.
_no_default: There is deliberately no palette-wide default terrain. The spec floated one
('terrain assumed when flags.terrain is absent'), but 530 tiles have no ground
surface because they ARE not ground — interiors, building footprints — and a
default would have painted every one of them concrete grey. Unpainted resolves
to null, and null means 'no terrain', not 'terrain unknown'.
_props_comment: props — the GAMEPLAY preset a tile inherits by being painted this terrain.
See docs/proposals/terrain-property-presets.md. Resolved at build into
zone_derived.props; a tile overrides any key with a flag of the same name.
A boolean override may be an explicit FALSE (absent = inherit, false = no):
a frozen bay is terrain water with swimmable:false, routable:true — still blue
on the map, walked across.
liquid      you are IN this tile, not ON it (fishing casts into it; the
overland void rim does not exist here). default false
swimmable   entering costs stamina; wetness, drowning, hypothermia. default false
underwater  submerged BELOW a surface tile: breath timer, colder, dark. default false
routable    GPS and pathfinding may cross it. default TRUE
buildable   the dev-panel builder may place/move a building here. default TRUE
frontage    a street a building front door may face onto. default false
speed_mult  movement pacing multiplier. default 1. Numeric, not boolean —
properties are typed by their default in PROP_DEFAULTS.
Only DIVERGENCE from the defaults is recorded, so a terrain with no props block
inherits everything — which is what most solid ground wants. marsh is deliberately
NOT liquid/swimmable: a marsh is walked, not swum (decision, 2026-07-30).
underwater shares water's minimap class and reads as the same substance; its
fill is a shade darker (#14283a against #1d3b52) because that is what the 82
tiles have always drawn — depth, seen from above. It used to share water's
fill exactly and the difference was carried per-tile; adopting the authored
value moved that distinction into the palette rather than inventing it. What
REALLY differs is what it does to you, not what it looks like.
